walkthrough:
**Identify what the molecule contains**

Look at the structure $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCOOH}$. It has an alkene $\text{C=C}$, a carbonyl $\text{C=O}$, a $\text{C-O}$ and an $\text{O-H}$ as part of the carboxylic acid $-\text{COOH}$ group.

So several bonds are present, we need the data to decide.

**Use the wavenumber and peak shape**

The spectrum shows a broad peak at 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$. Broadness is a famous clue in IR.

From the table:
$$\text{O-H (carboxyl) = 2500-3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}}$$

**Rule out the overlap and conclude**

It is true that $\text{C-H}$ (alkane) absorbs at 2850-2950 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, which lies inside this range. But $\text{C-H}$ gives a sharp peak, not a broad one.

Only the hydrogen-bonded $\text{O-H}$ of a carboxylic acid gives that very broad absorption over 2500-3000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, so the responsible bond is $\text{O-H}$.

options.A: C=C in an alkene absorbs at 1500-1680 cm-1. This is far below the observed 2500-3000 cm-1 range, so it cannot be responsible.
options.B: C=O in a carboxyl group absorbs at 1670-1740 cm-1. This is much lower wavenumber than the observed peak, so it is incorrect.
options.C: C-O absorbs at 1040-1300 cm-1. This is in the fingerprint region, far from 2500-3000 cm-1, so it cannot cause this peak.
options.D: O-H in a carboxyl group absorbs at 2500-3000 cm-1 and is characteristically broad due to strong hydrogen bonding. This matches both the position and shape perfectly for but-2-enoic acid.
